jobs.description:
Position Description

The City of Rochester welcomes applications for

GIS Specialist

Rochester Public Utilities

www.rpu.org

The City of Rochester is committed to a community where all members feel a sense of belonging. We commit to recognizing the diversity of our community members, listening to ALL
voices and providing equitable services to create an inclusive place to live, play and work.

We believe EQUITY
should be at the center of all our work. We strive to represent our community in our teammates, as we know that diverse and inclusive teams are more innovative, and have an empowering impact on the work, progress and culture of our community.

It takes us all working together

Nature of Work

This position develops, operates, and maintains enterprise GIS data, applications, and workflows. The GIS Specialist independently scopes and delivers assigned GIS solutions; performs spatial and database analysis; develops and maintains GIS applications and datasets; tests and documents technical work; supports users; and collaborates with internal staff, and partners. Work is performed using organizational standards and may include water, electric, infrastructure, field mobility, asset management, and other enterprise GIS applications.

Work Schedule
- The typical work schedule 8 AM - 5 PM Monday through Friday. Remote work is available up to two days a week after the first 6 months.

Pay
- The 2026 starting salary range is $85,632-$100,743 with advancement to $125,929.

Benefits
- This position is eligible for benefits offered by the City of Rochester. Please review the benefits tab at the top of the page for more details. Employees, whose new position with the City requires they relocate more than 50 miles, are eligible for relocation assistance, pursuant to City policy.

To have your application considered for the first round of interviews, please apply by Wednesday, October 7th, 2026, at 11:59 PM CST.

Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

The City of Rochester will not sponsor or transfer visas for this position including F1 OPT STEM.

Duties And Responsibilities

The work below is representative of the scope of work performed within this job classification. Individual job duties will vary based on work assignment . Support GIS administration and related technology.

Support GIS plans , systems, and solutions to meet Department needs .
Operate and maintain the enterprise GIS.
Assist in the development and administration of the departmental GIS work plan.
Independently scope, develop, test, document, and deliver assigned GIS applications, workflows, data products, and technical solutions.
Collaborate with customers, departments, and outside agencies to integrate GIS solutions with related systems and business processes.
Develop and maintain GIS applications that enhance efficiency and use of GIS.
Develop, maintain, and administer Department GIS data and databases.
Plan, develop, and administer spatial and attribute data sets.
Create and update public and associated private infrastructure GIS datasets?
Prepare and edit map layers and produce print or electronic maps for Engineering staff and others.?
Apply established policies and procedures for quality control and quality assurance.?
Develop and implement databases and applications for department records.?
Perform database administration, design SQL queries and perform data entry?
Support utility infrastructure management using field inventory data.?
Prepare and maintain documentation of data sources, database designs, data flows, and dataset metadata.
Test data processes and database changes; document results and coordinate implementation according to established change-management practices.
Provide public service to consultants, developers, citizens, and other agencies.
Work with other departments and governmental offices in developing and maintaining GIS databases for multiple users.
Respond to inquiries and requests for information about Department infrastructure.
Coordinate with other governmental GIS groups.
Prepare technical information for Boards, Councils, City staff agencies, Commissions, neighborhood groups, and professional organizations.
Provide training, guidance and technical support and provide guidance to department and division personnel on GIS, cartographic design, or other mapping requirements.
Provide training and technical support to internal GIS customers and other users of GIS data and applications.
Share technical knowledge, project status, risks, and dependencies with GIS team members so assigned solutions can be supported during staff absences and transitions.
Assist in developing budgets and schedules involving GIS applications, computer hardware and software.
Update, modify and expand GIS related sites including the ArcGIS Enterprise Portal.
Assist with hardware maintenance, software installation and maintenance, and troubleshoot system problems.

Perform Other Related Duties As Assigned

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor's degree in geographic information systems (GIS) or related field such as geography, planning, civil engineering, or computer science, with an emphasis in GIS coursework and training; AND three (3) years of full-time employment experience with geographic information systems mapping and database management using ESRI ArcGIS software or its equivalent

OR

An equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the job may also be considered.

If this work interests you but you are unsure if you meet all the job requirements listed above, please apply anyway! Your experience is likely more applicable to the role than you think, and the City is interested in candidates who can bring not only technical expertise but a variety of lived experience to the team.

Licenses and Certifications

Valid MN driver's license

Desirable Qualifications

Windows operating systems and Microsoft Office programs
Python programming skills
SQL Server database administration
ArcGIS Enterprise (Pro, Portal, Server) experience
Editing Utility Network data and branch versioning experience
Experience with mapping and/or survey grade GPS units
Experience with Schneider Electric’s ArcFM, Designer, Responder, and Fiber Manager Products

Additional Information

PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL CRITERIA

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the following represents the physical and environmental demands for this position. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions with or without accommodation.

In consideration of the overall amount of physical effort required to perform this position, the work is best described as Sedentary Work : Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time. Jobs are sedentary if walking and standing are required only occasionally and all other sedentary criteria are met.

that may be required continuously (2/3 or more of the time), frequently (1/3 to 2/3 of the time), and occasionally (up to 1/3 of the time) are noted below:

Continuous demands: sitting

Frequent demands: fine dexterity

Occasional demands: standing, walking, climbing, balancing, reaching, kneeling, crouching, crawling

Sensory requirements
necessary in the performance of the essential functions of this position include: sight, hearing, touch, taste and smell

Work is primarily performed indoors with no exposure to temperatures and external elements. Occasionally, work may be required outdoors and subject to the following factors:

Extreme cold (below 32 degrees)

Extreme heat (above 100 degrees)

Work outdoors (no effective protection from weather)

Work at heights (such as on scaffolding or ladders)

Walk on uneven ground (gravel, rocks, mounds, construction sites)

Job Title: Environmental Regulatory Specialist II

Location: Seattle, WA

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Currently HGL has a position open for an Environmental
Regulatory Specialist II
to work on environmental planning and permitting tasks for capital development projects. The position will support assignments that involve preparing NEPA documents, preparing applications and supporting materials for federal, state, and local environmental permits, regulatory agency coordination, coordination with tribes, and technical support to public engagement. The position will be based in HGL’s Seattle, WA office, but assignments will span nationwide geographic range. Business travel will be episodically needed and make up approximately 10% of the time for this position. This exciting role will provide opportunities for meaningful involvement in navigating the environmental process for large scale capital projects. The successful candidate will thrive in the role based on their knowledge of the environmental planning process, strategic thinking, ability to innovate, and proven writing skills.

Responsibilities/Duties

What You'll Be Doing

Document Preparation : Write and review NEPA planning documents (e.g., Categorical Exemptions, Environmental Assessments (EAs), and Environmental Impact Statements (EISs), and supporting technical discipline reports (as technically qualified).
Permit Application Preparation : Prepare environmental permit applications and supporting documents.
Impact Analysis : Analyze how proposed actions affect the natural environment (e.g., natural resources, wildlife) and the built environment (e.g., infrastructure, communities, economics).
Coordination with Design Teams : Interface with design engineers and technical specialists to align planning efforts and design efforts to obtain and incorporate information into environmental planning and permitting documents.
Client Interaction : Participate in meetings with clients as needed to support preparation of environmental planning and permitting documents.
Agency Coordination : Coordinate with federal, state, and local regulatory agencies and entities to secure environmental permits and approvals for proposed actions.
Public Engagement : Provide technical support for public engagement actions (e.g., public meetings, public notices, preparing responses to public comments).

Minimum Requirements

WHAT YOU NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL

The ideal candidate will need the following as a foundation for success in this role:

BA/BS in Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Biology, Environmental Planning, or related field.
Minimum 4+ years of directly related professional experience.
Experience preparing environmental planning documents for National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) compliance for capital projects.
Experience preparing permit applications for Clean Water Act Section 404 and 401 permits for capital projects.
Knowledge of Endangered Species Act (ESA) and Migratory Bird Treaty Act and experience supporting ESA Section 7 consultation for capital projects.
Expertise in a relevant technical discipline (e.g., ecology, wetlands, fisheries, environmental sciences). Wetlands expertise will be prioritized.
Professional competence with Microsoft Office (e.g., Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams) and SharePoint.
Demonstrated ability to learn and adopt new technologies and digital tools to improve project delivery and operational efficiency.

Desired Qualifications

WHAT YOU NEED TO STAND OUT – Preferred, not required

Working knowledge of CERCLA (Superfund) regulations, environmental cleanup actions, and application of environmental regulations in that context.
Experience with Applicable or Relevant and Appropriate Requirements (ARARs) analysis and documentation for CERCLA remediation planning and design.
Experience with mitigation planning and implementation for impacts to Waters of the United States (WOTUS).
Experience performing field reconnaissance and field data collection.
HAZWOPER 40-hour training/8-hour refresher.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIRMENTS

A bility to lift/move/relocate items up to 50 lbs.
Repetitive hand motions (typing, tool use, etc.)
Ability to see details at close range
Ability to see details at a distance
Viewing computer screen for extended periods
Ability to interpret and analyze visual data (maps, graphs, warning indicators, etc.)
Driving a company or personal vehicle
Analyzing and synthesizing data
Complex problem solving and decision making
Reading and interpreting technical documents or regulations
Writing reports, proposals, or technical documentation
Leading a team or coordinating multiple priorities
Communicating effectively with clients, team members, and stakeholders
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities

Work Environment Requirements

Must be able to travel up to 10% per year
May work in environments with loud noises, dust, or hazardous materials
Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE)
Office and remote work environment

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

Details

Work Schedule:
HGL office work is dictated by a 5-day work week; however, fieldwork schedules will deviate based on job requirements and may require longer hours and weekends.

Office Type
: In-office preferred, hybrid schedule available (3 days in office, 2 days remote)

Travel:
10%

A favorable pre-hire drug test is required.

All positions are subject to a pre-hire education and driving record verification.

MORE ABOUT HGL AND THE OPPORTUNITY

At HGL, we share a drive and vision to restore natural resources and provide ongoing stewardship of our environment to benefit present and future generations. We believe that we can make a difference in improving the world we live in through collaboration, teamwork, and a positive work environment. This unites and empowers us to strive for excellence in all our endeavors.

The exceptional quality of our people is key to our strength. We value our employees as individuals and as important members of our team. We offer a work environment that is flexible, inclusive, and dedicated to creating a sustainable future. With over 550 employees, HGL is large enough to execute high-profile projects, but small enough to develop personal working environments with our talented team members. By joining HGL, you will be working toward restoring the environment and protecting our future.

It’s not just a job, it’s your career. HGL provides career growth opportunities via mentoring, training, education, and support for your certifications and licenses. Achieve your career goals and help HGL achieve its mission of restoring the environment to beneficial use for our clients and communities.

EEO notices: US Equal Opportunity Employment Poster , US Equal Opportunity Supplemental Poster , Know Your Rights , and Pay Transparency Notice .

jobs.description:
Description

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The work of our Regional Environmental Engineers is critical to enabling AWS's growth in the US and around the world.

The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE), you will be responsible for environmental compliance at operating AWS data centers in Louisiana (SHV). You will develop standards and policies to support regulatory compliance, complete environmental performance analysis, establish and monitor metrics, and guide the teams in implementation of Amazon environmental standards. You will provide guidance and build effective relationships with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, design, construction, operations and other key stakeholders.

This position is based in Shreveport, Louisiana and will require travel throughout the state and the US.

Key job responsibilities

Manage and oversee compliance with environmental regulations and Amazon policy;
Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization;
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards;
Develop environmental metrics to measure, monitor and forecast performance;
Conduct thorough and accurate environmental audits for continuous improvement;
Prioritize and manage multiple technically complex assignments concurrently;
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company;
Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately;
Assist in time-critical compliance report submission to various governmental agencies;
Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and associated regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective action.

About The Team

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Why AWS?

AWS is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering
Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance programs including regulated waste, water, and air regulations in accordance with applicable laws
7+ years of experience in environmental compliance

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a data center or other critical environment
Experience with increasing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Mountainview Biological Consulting, LLC is a growing environmental consulting firm providing biological consulting services throughout California. We are seeking motivated professionals who are passionate about conservation and enjoy working in the field while contributing to meaningful environmental projects.

This is an excellent opportunity for biologists looking for flexible, part-time field work with opportunities for professional growth.

Mentorship and professional development with experienced environmental professionals.

jobs.title: Environmental Engineering - AI Data Trainer
jobs.description:
Environmental Engineering — AI Data Trainer

About The Role

We're looking for environmental engineering professionals to help train and improve cutting-edge AI models. Your domain expertise will directly shape how AI understands and reasons through complex environmental challenges — from contaminant transport to regulatory compliance.

This is a unique opportunity to apply your technical knowledge in a new way, working at the intersection of environmental science and artificial intelligence.

Organization: Alignerr
Type: Hourly Contract
Location: Remote
Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

What You'll Do

Design Complex Problems — Develop advanced environmental engineering challenges spanning contaminant transport, mass balance in treatment systems, hydrology, and Life Cycle Assessments (LCA)
Author Ground-Truth Solutions — Write rigorous, step-by-step technical solutions — including chemical dosage calculations, hydraulic flow models, and pollutant dispersion simulations — that serve as gold-standard reference responses
Audit AI Outputs — Evaluate AI-generated remediation plans, environmental impact statements, and mathematical reasoning for technical accuracy, safety, and regulatory compliance (EPA, ISO 14001, and others)
Refine AI Reasoning — Identify logical errors such as incorrect stoichiometry in biological processes or overlooked secondary environmental impacts, then provide structured feedback to improve how the model thinks
Work independently and asynchronously on your own schedule

Who You Are

Pursuing or holding a Master's or PhD in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering (environmental focus), or a closely related field
Strong foundational knowledge in one or more of: aquatic chemistry, wastewater process design, air quality engineering, or hazardous waste remediation
Skilled at communicating complex technical concepts clearly and precisely in writing
Detail-oriented — you catch unit conversion errors (mg/L vs. ppm), flawed chemical equations, and gaps in regulatory logic
No prior AI experience required

Who We Are

Flexcar is completely reimagining car ownership. We offer the world's first month-to-month car lease, with insurance and maintenance included. By combining operational expertise with technology, data, and AI, we are transforming every aspect of the customer journey and providing a smarter, more flexible alternative to traditional ownership. We're scaling fast — and we're building the next generation of leaders to scale with us.

Job Summary

We are seeking an Environmental Programs Manager to build and own environmental compliance across Flexcar's national network of vehicle hubs. Our operations generate regulated waste streams at every site, including used motor oil, coolant, brake fluid, detailing chemicals, waste tires, and 12V lead-acid batteries, along with stormwater, wash water, and chemical storage obligations that vary by state. You will own the environmental program end to end: setting the standards, holding the permits and registrations, managing waste vendors, serving as the company contact during agency inspections, and equipping our regional EHS Specialists to execute site-level environmental tasks day to day. This is a build role: the program does not exist yet in mature form, and you will be the person who creates it.

What You Will Do

National Environmental Program Ownership

Build and maintain Flexcar's environmental compliance program across all operating states, including written standards, site playbooks, and inspection checklists that regional EHS Specialists execute at their sites.
Own the national compliance calendar covering permits, registrations, renewals, inspections, sampling windows, and reporting deadlines, tracking corrective actions to verified closure.
Own environmental regulatory relationships nationally, serving as the company contact for agency inspections, information requests, and correspondence.
Conduct periodic environmental audits at sites across the network, and report environmental performance and open risks to Operations leadership.
Monitor state and federal regulatory changes affecting our operations and translate them into program updates before they become findings.

Hazardous, Universal, and Regulated Waste

Own generator classification and EPA identification across all sites, under federal RCRA and state programs, including California's Title 22 requirements, which regulate several of our streams more stringently.
Manage waste streams end to end at every site: used motor oil, coolant, brake fluid, detailing and cleaning chemicals, waste tires, and 12V lead-acid batteries, including characterization, accumulation and storage practices, container management and secondary containment, manifesting, and disposal.
Manage universal waste programs for 12V lead-acid batteries, aerosol cans, lamps, and electronics, including accumulation limits, labeling, and storage time rules under each state's program.
Maintain waste tire compliance state by state, including registered haulers, trip logs, and storage thresholds, covering CalRecycle requirements in California.
Apply used oil rules by state, including California's presumption that used oil is hazardous.
Qualify and manage waste haulers, disposal vendors, and environmental consultants nationally, including contracts, cost, and performance.

Water, Storage, and Site Conditions

Determine stormwater applicability at each site and maintain the resulting obligations, including industrial permit coverage or No Exposure Certification, SWPPPs and BMPs, sampling, annual evaluations, and state portal submittals.
Set standards for detailing and wash water handling across the network, including discharge authorization, clarifiers and interceptors, drain control, and dry cleanup practices.
Maintain aboveground storage tank compliance and SPCC plans where oil storage triggers applicability, including tank inspections, secondary containment, integrity and monitoring requirements under state programs, and spill containment readiness.
Manage EPCRA Tier II chemical inventory reporting where storage thresholds are met.
Maintain chemical inventory and SDS standards nationally, including approved-chemical controls.

California-Specific Programs

Maintain Hazardous Materials Business Plans, CERS reporting, and CUPA relationships for California sites, and serve as the site contact for CUPA inspections.
Maintain Prop 65 warning and exposure obligations.

Air Quality and Coating Operations (Planned Facility)

Lead air district permitting for the planned coating operation, including permit to construct, permit to operate, permit conditions, modifications, and renewals with the applicable district.
Establish compliance with the applicable district automotive coating rule and federal NESHAP 6H (40 CFR Part 63, Subpart HHHHHH), including VOC content limits, application equipment requirements, booth and filter standards, painter certification cycles, notifications, and recordkeeping.
Build the tracking for coating and solvent usage, VOC and HAP records, and emissions inventory and reporting where triggered, including AB 2588 obligations.
Add coating waste streams to the waste program, including waste paint, spent solvent, gun-cleaning waste, and contaminated booth filters, and reassess generator status accordingly.
Coordinate with Facilities and equipment vendors on environmental aspects of booth design and commissioning.

Environmental Incident Response

Own response to releases and spills across the network, including containment, cleanup, agency reporting within required timeframes, root cause investigation, and corrective action closure.

Training, Launches, and Facility Projects

Build environmental training content for site teams, including waste handling and segregation, spill response, and labeling, delivered through regional EHS Specialists and site leadership.
Serve as environmental reviewer for new site launches nationally, covering registrations, permits, waste program setup, and day-one readiness.
Provide environmental input on facility layout, chemical and waste storage, containment, and drainage during the design phase.

5+ years of environmental compliance experience, including California, in fleet, automotive service, manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or environmental consulting.

Working experience with stormwater permitting and SWPPPs, and with California CUPA, HMBP, and CERS obligations.

Join a diverse, dynamic, and enthusiastic team of environmental professionals who play a leading role in environmental permitting and compliance at Amazon Web Services (AWS), where we have a history of leading the world in innovative technologies and services. The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products. The team has responsibility for architecting and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs. This includes defining and implementing risk management and compliance systems and driving their continuous improvement; setting and refining global policies and procedures; overseeing the development of standards, tools, auditing and metrics, and employee training; ensuring effective engagement by environmental teams on global initiatives, including those that are part of Amazon’s ambitious sustainability goals; providing specialist expertise; and engaging with all AWS business units to provide scalable and effective compliance strategies that support current and future business objectives while ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

As a Regional Environmental Engineer (REE), you will be responsible for environmental compliance at operating AWS data centers in Louisiana (SHV). You will develop standards and policies to support regulatory compliance, complete environmental performance analysis, establish and monitor metrics, and guide the teams in implementation of Amazon environmental standards. You will provide guidance and build effective relationships with internal and external partners, including government entities, contractors, consultants, design, construction, operations and other key stakeholders.

This position is based in Shreveport, Louisiana and will require travel throughout the state and the US.

Key job responsibilities

Manage and oversee compliance with environmental regulations and Amazon policy;
Drive an environmentally responsible culture within the organization;
Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards;
Develop environmental metrics to measure, monitor and forecast performance;
Conduct thorough and accurate environmental audits for continuous improvement;
Prioritize and manage multiple technically complex assignments concurrently;
Represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies and throughout the company;
Build collaborative relationships with various stakeholders to ensure risks are identified early and managed appropriately;
Assist in time-critical compliance report submission to various governmental agencies;
Complete thorough and accurate environmental incident investigations and associated regulatory reports and develop appropriate corrective action.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Experience developing and implementing environmental compliance programs including regulated waste, water, and air regulations in accordance with applicable laws

Experience with increasing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, or service operations

Job Summary

We are seeking an Environmental Programs Manager to build and own environmental compliance across Flexcar's national network of vehicle hubs. Our operations generate regulated waste streams at every site, including used motor oil, coolant, brake fluid, detailing chemicals, waste tires, and 12V lead-acid batteries, along with stormwater, wash water, and chemical storage obligations that vary by state. You will own the environmental program end to end: setting the standards, holding the permits and registrations, managing waste vendors, serving as the company contact during agency inspections, and equipping our regional EHS Specialists to execute site-level environmental tasks day to day. This is a build role: the program does not exist yet in mature form, and you will be the person who creates it.

What You Will Do

National Environmental Program Ownership

Build and maintain Flexcar's environmental compliance program across all operating states, including written standards, site playbooks, and inspection checklists that regional EHS Specialists execute at their sites.
Own the national compliance calendar covering permits, registrations, renewals, inspections, sampling windows, and reporting deadlines, tracking corrective actions to verified closure.
Own environmental regulatory relationships nationally, serving as the company contact for agency inspections, information requests, and correspondence.
Conduct periodic environmental audits at sites across the network, and report environmental performance and open risks to Operations leadership.
Monitor state and federal regulatory changes affecting our operations and translate them into program updates before they become findings.

Hazardous, Universal, and Regulated Waste

Own generator classification and EPA identification across all sites, under federal RCRA and state programs, including California's Title 22 requirements, which regulate several of our streams more stringently.
Manage waste streams end to end at every site: used motor oil, coolant, brake fluid, detailing and cleaning chemicals, waste tires, and 12V lead-acid batteries, including characterization, accumulation and storage practices, container management and secondary containment, manifesting, and disposal.
Manage universal waste programs for 12V lead-acid batteries, aerosol cans, lamps, and electronics, including accumulation limits, labeling, and storage time rules under each state's program.
Maintain waste tire compliance state by state, including registered haulers, trip logs, and storage thresholds, covering CalRecycle requirements in California.
Apply used oil rules by state, including California's presumption that used oil is hazardous.
Qualify and manage waste haulers, disposal vendors, and environmental consultants nationally, including contracts, cost, and performance.

Water, Storage, and Site Conditions

Determine stormwater applicability at each site and maintain the resulting obligations, including industrial permit coverage or No Exposure Certification, SWPPPs and BMPs, sampling, annual evaluations, and state portal submittals.
Set standards for detailing and wash water handling across the network, including discharge authorization, clarifiers and interceptors, drain control, and dry cleanup practices.
Maintain aboveground storage tank compliance and SPCC plans where oil storage triggers applicability, including tank inspections, secondary containment, integrity and monitoring requirements under state programs, and spill containment readiness.
Manage EPCRA Tier II chemical inventory reporting where storage thresholds are met.
Maintain chemical inventory and SDS standards nationally, including approved-chemical controls.

California-Specific Programs

Maintain Hazardous Materials Business Plans, CERS reporting, and CUPA relationships for California sites, and serve as the site contact for CUPA inspections.
Maintain Prop 65 warning and exposure obligations.

Air Quality and Coating Operations (Planned Facility)

Lead air district permitting for the planned coating operation, including permit to construct, permit to operate, permit conditions, modifications, and renewals with the applicable district.
Establish compliance with the applicable district automotive coating rule and federal NESHAP 6H (40 CFR Part 63, Subpart HHHHHH), including VOC content limits, application equipment requirements, booth and filter standards, painter certification cycles, notifications, and recordkeeping.
Build the tracking for coating and solvent usage, VOC and HAP records, and emissions inventory and reporting where triggered, including AB 2588 obligations.
Add coating waste streams to the waste program, including waste paint, spent solvent, gun-cleaning waste, and contaminated booth filters, and reassess generator status accordingly.
Coordinate with Facilities and equipment vendors on environmental aspects of booth design and commissioning.

Environmental Incident Response

Own response to releases and spills across the network, including containment, cleanup, agency reporting within required timeframes, root cause investigation, and corrective action closure.

Training, Launches, and Facility Projects

Build environmental training content for site teams, including waste handling and segregation, spill response, and labeling, delivered through regional EHS Specialists and site leadership.
